identity.name: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
identity.chemical_class: Chemically modified starch (cross-linked hydroxypropylated starch phosphate)

function.mechanism: Hydrated modified starch polymer increases viscosity and water binding; hydroxypropyl/phosphate modifications improve process stability, while amylase can hydrolyze it and reduce viscosity.
common_food_categories: processed foods using food starch-modified under GMP

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI for modified starches including E1442.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern for reported uses/use levels in the general population; no numerical ADI needed.

fda.notes: Covered as food starch-modified with specified reagent/residual limits; not identified as a standalone GRAS listing in this CFR section.

adi.basis: JECFA record lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (2016 and earlier); 2018 entry was specification-only.

concerns.summary: An 89-week mouse feeding study with very high dietary inclusion reported mild renal/urinary findings (e.g., intratubular nephrosis) alongside GI enlargement, with partial reversibility after stopping exposure.
Rat studies reported reduced iron and zinc absorption in some hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate diet contexts.

Regulatory and experimental evidence indicates digestion by hydrolysis/fermentation rather than intact absorption; current concern is mainly physiological effects at high experimental exposures rather than established harm at normal use levels.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 found no safety concern at reported use levels and no need for a numerical ADI.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate.
1986 chronic mouse study did not provide evidence of carcinogenicity for hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is set by EFSA/JECFA for this additive category, so numeric ADI exceedance cannot be directly computed; EFSA reported no safety concern at reported use levels.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus (EFSA/JECFA/FDA framework) supports current uses with no numerical ADI, while older animal studies indicate some high-dose physiological effects and mineral-absorption caveats that justify continued monitoring but not high-risk classification.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no safety concern at reported uses; no numerical ADI needed
US regulation under 21 CFR 172.892 with use constraints
Older animal studies show mineral absorption and mild renal/GI effects under high experimental intakes
